title: EvoLib: Teaching LLMs to learn from experience
gist: Microsoft Research introduces EvoLib, a test-time learning framework that converts an LLM's own inference-time experience into an evolving library of reusable skills and reflective insights, refined via consolidation and long-horizon utility weighting. Because it requires no model updates, it works on any black-box API model, and it beats retrieval-based memory baselines on math, code and long-horizon agent tasks while using fewer tokens and converting test-time compute into gains faster.

insights.claim: Storing and retrieving past experiences is not the same as learning: an unstructured archive of conversations, reasoning traces and action histories grows so large that identifying the relevant knowledge for a new task becomes the bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Reframes the agent-memory category: vendors selling raw vector-store recall are solving retrieval, not learning, and may be positioned against the wrong problem.
insights.quote: Memory has become an important AI agent capability: the ability to store and retrieve past experiences. But memory alone is not learning.
insights.locator: Memory has become an important AI agent

insights.claim: The design template is explicitly human cognition: people discard most detail and retain only strategies that work, mistakes to avoid, and skills that transfer, refining them into increasingly general knowledge.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Signals where agent-memory research is heading — lossy abstraction over lossless logging — which favors architectures that compress rather than ones that index everything.
insights.quote: Humans learn differently. We do not remember every detail of our past experiences.

insights.claim: EvoLib's unit of storage is not a raw experience but a knowledge unit that is either a reusable skill distilled from a successful solution or a reflective insight learned from a mistake.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: A concrete data-structure spec competitors can copy; the moat is in the extraction and evolution policy, not the store.

themes.theme: Consolidation and long-horizon weighting as the evolution mechanism

insights.claim: When new knowledge is extracted, EvoLib retrieves similar existing entries and merges them into a more general, reusable unit, so knowledge moves beyond the individual experience that produced it.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Consolidation is what caps context and token growth as experience accumulates — the economics of long-lived agents depend on this step.
insights.locator: Consolidation. As new knowledge is extracted

insights.claim: Each knowledge unit is reweighted not only by its immediate utility on the current task but by how much it contributes to generating useful knowledge on future tasks, a credit-assignment scheme that promotes compounding knowledge over locally handy knowledge.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: The non-obvious design choice in the paper: valuing knowledge by its downstream generativity is what turns a memory store into an appreciating asset.

insights.claim: Learning is fully self-supervised at inference time, requiring neither ground-truth labels nor external feedback to extract and refine knowledge from the model's own attempts.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Removes the labeled-data dependency that gates most continual-learning deployments; the constraint becomes inference compute, not annotation budget.
insights.locator: Self-supervised. EvoLib enables large language models

themes.theme: Test-time compute efficiency and benchmark results

insights.claim: Across mathematical reasoning, code writing under efficiency constraints, and long-horizon environment interaction, EvoLib consistently outperforms the top retrieval-based memory approaches and other abstract memory mechanisms while using fewer tokens.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Beating retrieval baselines on both accuracy and token cost simultaneously is the rare result that survives a procurement review.
insights.locator: Across these tasks, EvoLib consistently outperforms

insights.claim: On all three benchmarks EvoLib sits above both isolated compute-scaling methods and strong memory-based learning approaches across most of the test-time compute range, and its performance curve rises more steeply as compute increases.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: A steeper compute-to-performance slope is the metric that matters for inference-heavy products: it changes the unit economics of every additional GPU-second.
insights.locator: Across all three benchmarks, EvoLib achieves

insights.claim: The results imply that neither storing more memories nor spending more compute is the primary lever; the gain comes from converting experience into reusable knowledge that is continually refined across tasks.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: A direct challenge to the brute-force test-time-scaling narrative, and a hint that algorithmic memory design can substitute for compute spend.
insights.quote: These results suggest that the key to better learning may not simply be storing more memories or spending more compute.
insights.locator: These results suggest that the key

insights.claim: Performance stays stable when the same heterogeneous task set is presented in different random orders, showing the framework does not depend on a structured curriculum.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Order-robustness is what makes this deployable against a real production stream of mixed user requests rather than a curated eval set.

insights.claim: Because EvoLib never updates model weights, it can be layered onto any black-box language model or AI system reached only through an API.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Model-agnostic by construction: value accrues to the orchestration layer, not the weights, which cuts against fine-tuning-based differentiation.
insights.quote: As EvoLib does not require model updates, it can be applied to any black-box language models and AI systems deployed through APIs.

insights.claim: The team frames the trajectory of AI progress as depending not only on larger models and more computation but on mechanisms for continually accumulating, refining and reusing knowledge, as systems take on longer-running and more complex tasks.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Microsoft Research is publicly hedging the pure-scaling thesis, which matters for how it allocates between capex on training clusters and inference-side research.
insights.quote: The future of AI may depend not only on larger models and more computation, but also on mechanisms that allow systems to continually accumulate, refine, and reuse knowledge.
insights.locator: As AI systems take on longer-running

insights.claim: Code and experiment results are released on GitHub to seed outside research on memory and knowledge evolution, rather than being held as a proprietary agent feature.
insights.speaker: Microsoft Research
insights.so_what: Open-sourcing the method suggests Microsoft expects the durable advantage to be in products and distribution, not in the memory algorithm itself.
